questions.question: A person can complete 1/4th of a job in 2 hours. How long will it take for the same person to complete 3/4th of the job?
questions.explanation: Since the person completes 1/4th of the job in 2 hours, the total time to complete 3/4th of the job will be 6 hours.

questions.question: If two pipes are connected together, one filling a tank at 1/8th of a tank per hour and the other at 1/12th of a tank per hour, then how long will it take to fill the tank completely?
questions.explanation: The combined rate of filling the tank is 1/8 + 1/12 = 5/24 per hour.

questions.question: A man can finish 1/2 of a job in 5 hours. His son can finish the same job in 10 hours. How long will it take for both of them working together to finish the job?
questions.explanation: Their combined rate of work is 1/5 + 1/10 = 3/10 per hour.

questions.question: A water pump can fill 1/6th of a tank in 2 hours. How long will it take to fill 3 tanks?
questions.explanation: The pump fills 1/6th of a tank in 2 hours, so it will fill 3 tanks in 6 * 3 = 18 hours.

questions.question: A group of workers can complete a job in 12 days. If 1/3rd of the workers are absent, then how many days will it take to complete the job?
questions.explanation: Since 1/3rd of the workers are absent, the remaining workers will take 12 / (2/3) = 18 days to complete the job.

questions.question: A train covers a distance of 480 km between Kolkata and Durgapur in 8 hours. How much time will it take to cover a distance of 240 km?
questions.explanation: Speed remains constant.

questions.question: A car travels from Siliguri to Darjeeling, a distance of 98 km, in 4 hours. How much time will it take to travel a distance of 196 km?
questions.explanation: Time is directly proportional to the distance.

questions.question: A person travels from Kolkata to Howrah by ferry. The speed of the ferry is 30 km/h. How much time will it take to cover a distance of 15 km?
questions.explanation: Time is inversely proportional to the speed.

questions.question: A bus travels from Asansol to Dhanbad at an average speed of 60 km/h. If the total distance is 144 km, how much time will it take to reach Dhanbad?
questions.explanation: Time is directly proportional to the distance.

questions.question: A train leaves Sealdah station at 9:00 AM and reaches Bardhaman at 12:30 PM. If the distance between the two cities is 150 km, what is the average speed of the train?
questions.explanation: Average speed is distance divided by time.

questions.explanation: The pattern continues alphabetically.

questions.explanation: The code is a repetition of the number.

questions.explanation: The pattern continues alphabetically with a shift of 2.

questions.question: Amar is the son of Bhairab's son, who is the son of Kumar. How is Amar related to Kumar?
questions.explanation: Amar is Kumar's grandson.

questions.question: Rahul's mother is the mother of Sumanta. What is the relationship between Rahul and Sumanta?
questions.explanation: Rahul and Sumanta are father-son.

questions.question: A person is the mother of a male, who is the husband of a female. What is the relationship between the person and the female?
questions.explanation: The person is the female's sister.

questions.question: If I am the brother of your wife, what am I to your sister?
questions.explanation: I am your sister's nephew.

questions.question: Srijan is the father of the wife of a man. How is Srijan related to that man?
questions.explanation: Srijan is the man's father.

questions.question: If I am standing at the Howrah Bridge and face the River Hooghly, which direction will I face if I turn 180 degrees and walk for 400 meters?
questions.explanation: Because 180-degree turn will face the opposite direction of the initial position.

questions.question: If I start from the Dakshineswar Kali Temple and walk 250 meters towards the east, then 150 meters towards the north, and finally 300 meters towards the west, which direction am I facing?
questions.explanation: Because north-south movement will cancel out the east-west movement.

questions.question: If I am at the Park Street Metro Station and move 200 meters towards the north, then 150 meters towards the east, and finally 300 meters towards the south, which direction am I facing?
questions.explanation: Because north-south movement will cancel out the east-west movement.

questions.question: If I am at the Kalighat Temple and face the Kalighat Temple's main gate. If I turn 90 degrees to my right, then 90 degrees to my left, which direction am I facing?
questions.explanation: Because turning 90 degrees to the right and then 90 degrees to the left makes a total of 180-degree turn.

questions.question: I am at the Esplanade Bus Stand. If I move 100 meters towards the west and then 200 meters towards the north, which direction am I facing?
questions.explanation: Because north-south movement has no effect on east-west movement.
